approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules. It chooses parents from high-scoring population quantiles and fills a surplus pool using connected-fragment crossover or successive local mutations, with bounded retries and saturation recovery. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities and duplicate rejection govern pool admission. A Gaussian posterior trained on the full accepted archive uses integer-count Morgan fingerprints and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated score draws select distinct candidates from the pool. Accepted feedback updates the archive and a bounded population of the best observed molecules.
approach.novelty: Add a narrow sulfur-environment introduction gate at final pool admission. It preserves the source experiment's neutral sulfur envelope and exact local signatures, including permitted terminal carbon-sulfur double bonds. For a one-parent proposal, outside-envelope signature counts may not exceed that parent's counts. For crossover, each signature may not exceed its largest count in either actual generating parent. Rejected products trigger the existing bounded refill loop. The new question is transfer from a single-source tabu walk to two-parent graph pools with posterior selection. Completed siblings altered crossover or posterior components; pending siblings alter donor construction or ordinary continuation. This Child retains those Parent mechanisms and tests only the sulfur admission rule.

hypothesis: Reject a final valid canonically novel offspring before pool admission exactly when an outside-envelope sulfur local signature has greater multiplicity than its maximum across the actual accepted scored generating parents, using the fixed neutral-sulfur envelope and exact signature from n-93cd9a000278, then continue the inherited bounded pool-generation loop.

finding_summary.headline: The sulfur gate contains new violations and retains the mean, but misses the performance-gain goal
finding_summary.insights: The narrow admission rule transfers from a single-source walk to scored-parent pools and can preserve the panel mean without establishing a useful endpoint gain. Its real exposure is sparse and uneven, and the Parent included one targeted introduction that improved its incumbent, so rejecting this chemistry is not synonymous with removing only unproductive paths. The exact per-signature maximum is validated separately from a parental sum; synthetic boundary cases are not search evidence. The relative rule would still allow inherited signatures within their reference counts: an inherited outside-envelope Parent offspring became the deco_hop incumbent at 0.617802. Zero absolute violations here therefore does not establish universal cleanliness. The emitted chemistry retains permitted thiocarbonyls, thioethers and oxides, but also 93 sulfur-halogen observations and unresolved non-sulfur reactivity, ring geometry and stereochemistry. Conventional thioether and sulfur-free improving alternatives constrain those concerns without proving a broader filter would help. The earlier source gate still has its favorable mean alongside a losing seed and greater dispersion; this new result neither pools nor rewrites that evidence.
finding_summary.results: The gate rejects exactly 130 of 69730 valid novel pool candidates with positive sulfur-signature excess. All 69,600 admitted members and 4,350 evaluated offspring have zero excess against their actual scored parents. Rejections affect 81 batches containing 810 real accepted evaluations; every pool and announced batch completes. 3 sessions have no positive exposure and reproduce their Parent trajectories. Absolute outside-envelope sulfur also falls from seven Parent emissions to zero Child emissions under these clean inherited states, while sulfur remains in 1100 Child observations versus 935 Parent observations. Mean endpoint score rises from 0.595670 to 0.596453, a change of only +0.000783. That meets the registered -0.002 noninferiority boundary but misses the separate +0.002 gain goal. Seed changes are +0.017686, +0.002307 and -0.017643; six task-seed endpoints improve, six decline and three tie. Macro population dispersion rises from 0.026593 to 0.033970.

molecular.headline: Sulfur stays inside the narrow envelope; aromatic leaders still carry reactive attachments and difficult ring geometry

There is substantial ring and aromatic chemistry, with narrower leader families within seeds. Digest ring-closure-string incidence ranges from 0.9598 to 0.9897 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.9517 to 0.9782. Those are molecule-level text incidences, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout, although aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic centres are plainly present. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory paths were present and read, covering all five objectives and issued Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. Each node has 900 records per objective, including 870 accepted optimizer observations. No path, task or paired seed comparison is missing. context.comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with no profile mismatch; the baseline is the published current-profile n-62daf219c70a. The full records, not only the digest late seed-2 proposals, establish the seed endpoints. The entire 300-record sessions for zaleplon_mpo seed 1, deco_hop seed 0 and median_2 seed 1 reproduce Parent evaluation/source/SMILES/score/best_so_far records exactly. Other sessions diverge chemically; exact endpoint ties alone were not used to claim identity. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 classification using the brief's declared neutral sulfur cases finds no absolute outside-envelope sulfur centres in the initial molecules or any of the 4350 Child optimizer observations. Parent has seven such optimizer observations, all in seed 2: three terminal nitrogen-sulfur-double cases in deco_hop, two unusual sulfur-valence cases in drd2_docking, and two in median_2. This is an absolute output description, not a reconstruction of parent-relative excess, rejection decisions or mechanism activation. The declared relative rule permits inherited outside-envelope signatures within their reference multiplicities; zero observed here is conditional on these trajectories and cannot be generalized to other starting populations. Sulfur is not removed: 1100 Child optimizer observations contain sulfur versus 935 Parent observations. Child sulfur centre counts are 734 divalent/hydrogen-bearing, 11 aromatic, 299 terminal carbon-double, 71 one-oxo and 86 two-oxo. These correspond respectively to 688, 11, 291, 71 and 77 molecule observations; a molecule can contain several centres or classes. The envelope permits sulfur-halogen bonds, N-S connections and thiocarbonyl groups, and constrains no non-sulfur atom. It establishes neither universal plausibility nor stability, safety, synthesis, pharmacology or geometry. Reactive local bonding, small-ring/bridged unsaturation and unspecified stereochemistry therefore keep overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak, despite recognizable high-scoring azaaryl amides and cyclic aryl amines. Molecular sizes, motif counts and path hashes are documented in .slots/r0016-03-improve-L01/molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
